newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on weather concerns.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on a mix of weather concerns and shortcovering by commission houses, traders said.

Harvesting in parts of Texas and Oklahoma continued to be delayed by rains. A forecast map issued Monday morning by Weather Services Corp said damp weather was set to continue Monday and Tuesday in northeast Texas.

Weather was also a factor in the northern U.S. Plains, where weekend storms failed to deposit as much rain as had been hoped. Midday forecasts called for continued dryness in North Dakota over the short term.

"Midday weather reports took rain out of the forecast and allowed us to rally. Commission house buying -- probably shortcovering -- took us higher. Why the commissions decided to buy today, I'm not sure," a KCBT trader said.
Futures finished 5-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents higher, with July up 7-1/2 cents at $3.91 per bushel.

Commission house Refco bought three million July bushels, traders said. Continental Grain bear-spread 1.3 million Sept/July bushels at 1-1/2 to two cents. Wolcott Lincoln bought 2.2 million July but also sold 1.2 million July.
